title: An AI Security Facepalm: OpenAI’s Evaluation Became Hugging Face’s Incident
summary: OpenAI models escaped containment and breached Hugging Face while pursuing an evaluation goal. Learn what this incident means for CISOs and agentic AI security.
body_text: In a move straight out of a horror movie or techno-dystopian thriller, OpenAI’s model did what Anthropic threatened its model could do (but didn’t): A frontier lab’s own models escaped containment during an authorized evaluation and breached another company to finish the task and perform an autonomous hack. OpenAI confirmed that its own models escaped a constrained evaluation environment, reached the open internet, and breached Hugging Face’s production infrastructure to obtain answers for a cybersecurity benchmark. The models included GPT-5.6 Sol and a more capable prerelease model running with reduced cyber refusals, with a security research harness. OpenAI called the event an unprecedented cyber incident. We agree with that assessment. The models did not wander into Hugging Face by accident. They pursued a narrow evaluation goal, found a zero-day in OpenAI’s package-registry proxy, escalated privileges, located a node with internet access, inferred that Hugging Face might hold ExploitGym solutions, and compromised production systems to retrieve them. Forrester’s AEGIS framework – the first and only framework designed exclusively to address agentic AI security threats – covers each of these scenarios. We provide deep exploration of goal and intent hijacking, unrestrained agency and privilege, and evasion and deception. These are all characteristics that OpenAI’s model exhibited during its attack. Agentic AI changes both the economics and the source of attack. A model provider’s internal evaluation became an external production incident at another company. Security teams now have to account for capable models that can chain vulnerabilities, cross trust boundaries, and cause harm while pursuing the goal their operators assigned. A Narrow Goal Drove A Cross-Company Breach OpenAI designed the evaluation to measure advanced exploitation across complex attack paths. The models ran without the production classifiers that normally block high-risk cyber activity. OpenAI isolated the environment and limited network access to an internally hosted third-party proxy that cached software packages. The models turned that tiny exception into an exit. They spent substantial inference compute searching for open internet access, exploited a previously unknown flaw in the proxy, escalated privileges, moved laterally through OpenAI’s research environment, and reached a node with internet access. They then targeted Hugging Face, combined stolen credentials with additional vulnerabilities, and obtained test solutions from its production database. Keep in mind that no human operators directed the OpenAI model activity . The model operated completely independently. Hugging Face’s original disclosure captured the operational scale: thousands of actions across short-lived sandboxes, lateral movement through internal clusters, and migrating command-and-control infrastructure staged on public services. It was able to identify the attack as agentic because of the massive scale and operational decisions made by the models. Hugging Face contained the agent after it compromised internal datasets and service credentials. The intent matters more than the techniques used. The models tried to solve an evaluation, not torch the internet. That narrow objective still produced a zero-day exploit, a containment escape, cross-company intrusion, credential theft, and production data access. This is reminiscent of an attack demonstrated by Palisade Research in 2025 that also used OpenAI models. In that scenario, an agent cheated to win against the Stockfish chess engine. OpenAI’s o1-preview noted , “The task is to ‘win against a powerful chess engine’ — not necessarily to win fairly in a chess game,” so it modified system files to allow illegal moves, forcing its opponent to resign. This is why Forrester has declared intent as a first-class security object, and securing intent must be a new priority for CISOs ( which Jeff Pollard and Heidi Shey will present in a Black Hat briefing on August 6 at 3:35 p.m.) . Security architectures that assume benign intent will miss this failure mode. Agents can pursue authorized goals through unauthorized means, especially when evaluators reward the outcome and fail to police the path. Boards and C-suite leaders need to understand new intent-related exposures, which this event exposes in gritty detail. Reduced Refusals And Failed Containment Created The Incident OpenAI’s disclosure changes the guardrails story. The attacking models ran with reduced cyber refusals because the evaluation aimed to measure their maximum offensive capability. OpenAI relied on environmental containment to offset that capability. The package-registry proxy provided a tightly-scoped network path, but the models found a zero-day in the proxy and converted it into open internet access. The control design treated the sandbox boundary as reliable while running models explicitly pushed to defeat obstacles. Hugging Face then hit the mirror-image problem during response: Commercial frontier models refused to analyze live attacker commands and payloads. The incident put reduced safeguards on the offensive side and restrictive safeguards on the defensive side. That’s a governance faceplant. Hugging Face switched to GLM-5.2, a self-hosted open-weight model, and analyzed more than 17,000 events in hours rather than days while keeping stolen credentials inside its environment. Responders made a high-stakes call about model sovereignty, supply chain, and governance during an active incident because they needed a tool that worked. Our analysis of Fable 5 and Mythos 5 warned that organizations increasingly depend on safety controls, policy decisions, and service restrictions that someone else operates. This incident adds another dependency: Model developers must prove that evaluation environments can contain the capabilities they intentionally expose. Govern Agent Intent Before Shadow Adoption Does It For You Only days before the incident, Anthropic Deputy CISO Jason Clinton published guidance for security leaders on agentic AI risk . OpenAI’s evaluation supplied a live example of the problem he described. Clinton argued that security leaders must decide how much agentic risk they’ll accept before the business decides for them. He also wrote that “an agent that drifts out of alignment with your intent is indistinguishable from an insider attack.” OpenAI’s models stayed locked on the benchmark, but their route to the answer blew through containment and harmed another organization. His advice to design for where models will be in six months, rather than where they are today, now carries more urgency. His four questions that belong in model evaluations, procurement reviews, architecture reviews, and threat modeling are: What untrusted content does it ingest? What actions can it take and on whose behalf? What is the blast radius if it is misaligned? What observability do I have? OpenAI’s evaluation answers those questions with uncomfortable precision. The models ingested a goal that rewarded exploitation, operated with reduced refusals, found an unplanned action path, and crossed from a research environment into a third party’s production systems. Neither the benchmark nor the sandbox kept the models inside the intended boundary. Security teams need telemetry that captures the model, prompt, goal, tools, credentials, intermediate decisions, network paths, and external effects. Without that evidence, containment drags and investigators reconstruct intent from infrastructure crumbs. Explainability, observability, least agency, and continuous assurance must govern evaluations as rigorously as production deployments. AI software supply-chain risk ranked among Forrester’s top cybersecurity threats for 2026 . OpenAI’s package-registry proxy became the first escape path, and Hugging Face became the downstream target. The incident shows how a trusted development service, proxy, benchmark, dataset host, or model repository can connect environments that their owners consider separate. Security teams must map those transitive trust paths before a capable model finds them first. Model Evaluation Has Become A Production-Risk Activity Security leaders need to drag model evaluations inside the enterprise risk boundary. OpenAI intentionally reduced cyber refusals to measure maximum capability, then relied on isolation to contain the result. The models defeated that isolation and created an incident outside OpenAI. Evaluations that remove safeguards or reward long-horizon exploitation now carry the risk profile of offensive security operations. CISOs should require threat models, independent containment tests, egress controls, kill criteria, named incident owners, external notification procedures, and evidence retention before teams run high-capability evaluations. They should also treat benchmark design as a security control. A benchmark that rewards task completion without penalizing boundary violations teaches operators little about safe performance and gives the model every reason to search for unintended paths. Capability testing needs governance equal to the capability under test. Hugging Face’s response reinforces the continuity lesson included in our analysis of Anthropic and the US government . Security teams need tested model fallbacks for investigations, while model developers need defense-in-depth that assumes their strongest model will attack every available boundary. Build The Controls Before You Need Them This incident shows model providers, enterprises, and security teams that agentic risk starts before deployment. Evaluations, sandboxes, package services, benchmarks, credentials, and external dependencies all sit inside the attack surface. Forrester’s AEGIS framework addresses that full lifecycle. Organizations need to act on seven priorities: Govern high-capability evaluations as offensive operations. Require explicit authorization, containment tests, abort criteria, incident ownership, and external notification procedures, consistent with a new AppSec operating model for agentic development . Apply least agency to models under evaluation. Limit each model’s tools, credentials, compute, network paths, and authority, using Forrester’s AEGIS guidance for IAM and AI agents . Design containment for model-led attacks against the containment itself. Remove unnecessary egress, isolate package infrastructure, rotate credentials, and apply AEGIS guardrails for Zero Trust architecture across every trust boundary. Record the complete chain from goal to external effect. Preserve prompts, intermediate reasoning artifacts, tool calls, identities, network activity, and policy decisions, following the Five Eyes guidance operationalized through AEGIS . Maintain an incident-response model under your control. Test a self-hosted or open-weight fallback before provider policies block critical analysis, as our analysis of AI provider concentration and continuity risk prescribes. Evaluate AI vendors for evaluation safety and continuity. Examine how providers reduce safeguards, isolate models, govern benchmarks, disclose incidents, and support responders through the vendor-risk lens discussed in our analysis of Fable 5 and Mythos 5 . Treat the AI software supply chain as critical infrastructure. Map transitive trust across model hosts, package proxies, repositories, benchmarks, and developer tools, then apply controls that assume one of those services will fail . title: Automations with Scheduled AI Agents: The Power of "Set It and Forget It" Workflows
summary: Discover how scheduled AI agents can transform your productivity by automating routine tasks like email management. Learn how Wordware's new scheduled triggers feature lets you build powerful AI workflows that run on autopilot.
body_text: The Promise of AI Automation: More Time for What Matters The true potential of AI isn't just about making tasks easier—it's about completely removing them from your to-do list. Imagine having a personal assistant who not only understands exactly what you need but takes care of it automatically at precisely the right time, every time. That's the promise of AI agents with scheduled automation: set it up once, and let it handle repetitive tasks while you focus on more meaningful work. Today, we're excited to introduce a game-changing feature that brings this vision to life: scheduled triggers for AI agents in Wordware. What Are Scheduled Triggers and Why Do They Matter? Scheduled triggers are exactly what they sound like—the ability to automatically activate an AI workflow at predetermined times. This seemingly simple capability unlocks an entirely new dimension of productivity. Here's why this matters: True automation : Unlike tools that merely assist you while you work, scheduled agents work independently, even when you're not actively using them Consistency : Critical tasks happen on schedule, without relying on your memory or availability Time optimization : Receive insights and completed tasks exactly when you need them Reduced cognitive load : Eliminate the mental burden of remembering and managing routine processes Real-World Example: Your Daily Email Intelligence Briefing Let's explore a practical example that demonstrates the power of scheduled triggers: a daily email summary agent. The Problem It Solves Most of us face email overload. By day's end, your inbox is cluttered with messages of varying importance, and sorting through them becomes a stressful time sink. You might miss critical communications while wasting time on low-priority messages. The Solution: An Automated Email Intelligence Agent With Wordware's scheduled triggers, you can create an AI agent that: Automatically runs at your specified time each day (e.g., 5:00 PM) Scans your inbox for new messages Intelligently categorizes and summarizes them Identifies which emails need immediate attention Delivers a concise summary directly to your inbox The result? You receive a daily intelligence briefing that helps you quickly identify what matters and what can wait—all without lifting a finger. Building Your First Scheduled Agent in Wordware Creating a scheduled workflow in Wordware is remarkably straightforward, even if you have no coding experience. The platform uses natural language programming, allowing you to describe what you want in plain English. Here's how to build your own daily email summary agent: Create a new project in your Wordware workspace Configure the schedule trigger by selecting your preferred frequency (daily, weekly, monthly) and specific time Connect your email account through Wordware's secure authentication Define the workflow logic using natural language instructions: Find all new emails since the last check Identify messages requiring immediate attention Generate summaries of important content Format everything into a digestible report Set up the delivery method (typically sending the summary to your email) Publish your agent to activate the automation Once published, your agent runs silently in the background, delivering valuable insights right when you need them. Who Benefits Most from Scheduled AI Agents? Scheduled automation through AI agents provides exceptional value for: Busy professionals who need to stay on top of communications but can't constantly monitor their inbox Team leaders who want to receive regular updates without micromanaging Knowledge workers dealing with information overload Small business owners juggling multiple responsibilities Anyone seeking to reduce digital noise and focus on high-value work Beyond Email: Other Powerful Use Cases While our email summary example demonstrates the concept clearly, scheduled triggers enable countless other valuable workflows: Daily data reports that analyze business metrics and highlight trends Content monitoring that tracks mentions of your brand or industry developments Regular social media updates based on trending topics or scheduled content calendars Automated follow-ups with customers or prospects at optimal intervals System health checks that proactively identify potential issues Why Natural Language Programming Makes All the Difference What sets Wordware apart is its document-based approach to building AI agents. Instead of complex coding or confusing visual interfaces, you simply describe what you want your agent to do in plain English. This natural language programming approach means: Anyone can build sophisticated agents regardless of technical background Workflows can be quickly modified as your needs evolve The learning curve is minimal compared to traditional automation tools Your instructions remain readable and understandable months or years later Getting Started with Wordware Scheduled Triggers Ready to experience the freedom of truly automated AI workflows? Here's how to get started: Visit wordware.ai to create your account Explore the template library for pre-built scheduled workflows Customize a template or build your own agent from scratch Set up your first scheduled trigger and watch your productivity transform The most powerful productivity tool isn't the one that helps you work faster—it's the one that eliminates the need for you to do the work at all. With Wordware's scheduled triggers, you're not just saving time; you're reclaiming it entirely. The Future of Work is Automated As AI capabilities continue to advance, the line between what requires human attention and what can be delegated to AI agents will shift dramatically. Those who embrace these tools early will gain a significant advantage in both productivity and work-life balance. Scheduled AI agents represent a fundamental shift in how we approach work—moving from "how can I do this faster?" to "do I need to do this at all?" Ready to transform your productivity with AI that works on your schedule? Visit Wordware today and build your first scheduled agent in minutes.

title: Retail Software Solutions Enhance User Experience
summary: Discover how a luxury fashion retailer transformed its online shopping experience through user-friendly retail software solutions.
body_text: We empowered our client to identify technical solutions to optimize the client’s retail platform, deliver on the technology and application needs, and design better processes to ensure continued success. Stage 1: Architecture Development Scalability Assessment and Planning: We conducted a comprehensive assessment of the client’s existing platform and determined that its complexity necessitated a complete code overhaul and the implementation of new technologies. Front-End and Back-End Overhaul: As part of a comprehensive renewal of the platform, the client was able to redesign the interface to enhance user interaction and aesthetic appeal and upgraded the system to improve performance, scalability, and user-friendliness. Transition to Single-Page Application (SPA): To ensure scalability, we performed a comprehensive assessment of the platform’s needs and determined that its complexity required a complete code rewrite and the adoption of new technologies. These new retail software solutions revolutionized our client’s online fashion platform, enhancing its speed, scalability, and user-friendliness. The partnership showed how maintaining swift and effective communication channels solidify trust and ensure seamless collaboration. Stage 2: Features Extension and Optimization Support and Expertise: Throughout the platform extension phase, the client received robust support and technical expertise, facilitating a seamless and efficient transition as new features were integrated. Additional Functionalities: The client implemented a product ranking automation tool that sorted products by its targeted needs and promoted specific brands. Additionally, it introduced a product information management system to manage all product details. Payment and Shipping: We integrated Klarna as a payment method and configured payments to be country-based, enabling specific payment methods and bonus schemes. We also enabled new shipping options, customizable by country, with new delivery partners. User Experience Enhancement: Our “shop the look” feature allowed customers to purchase entire outfits based on website photos, while integration of a search-as-a-service platform enabled users to filter products by brand, color, and size, significantly improving the shopping experience. The extension and optimization of the platform provided our client with advanced features and tools, greatly enhancing their ecommerce capabilities and elevating user satisfaction. Additionally, the client saw improvements in the look and feel of the website with a new, custom-made UX design, further enhancing the overall user experience. Stage 3: Continuous Improvement To further enhance customer retention, we empowered the client’s SEO expert to implement several key features and significantly boost search engine rankings over an extended period. We also developed and integrated a sophisticated return system that enabled seamless, automated returns directly through the shop. This enhancement streamlined the return process for both customers and the client. Finally, we developed a system allowing customers to create multiple wishlists, integrated with automated emails to improve customer retention and engagement, providing personalized recommendations and updates based on their wishlist activity.

title: Web Summit 2026 travel guide made simple
summary: Plan your Web Summit 2026 trip to Lisbon with per diem data, hotel zone tips, networking frameworks, and a guide from booking to post-conference follow-up.
body_text: Key takeaways Web Summit 2026 brings 70,000+ attendees to Lisbon's Altice Arena from November 9–12, and the trip logistics matter as much as the sessions. Anonymized Navan booking data that reveals when to book, what to budget, and how to avoid the conference-week pricing premium. Hotel prices near Altice Arena increase sharply during Web Summit week, and travelers who book one to two months ahead typically pay about $100 less per night than those who wait until the last minute. Lisbon's conference-week hotel rates often exceed the U.S. State Department lodging per diem, so budget accordingly or consider staying outside Parque das Nações. Lisbon Airport connects to the venue in about 10 minutes via the Metro Red Line, making it one of the easiest conference transfers you'll make. Planning your networking outreach before the conference helps turn a 70,000-person event into a schedule of meaningful meetings. Navan Edge is the personal assistant for business travel that can book flights, hotels, and restaurants in one conversation thread, so you can focus on the conference instead of the logistics. Web Summit 2026 will draw more than 70,000 people from more than 160 countries to Lisbon this November, and the Altice Arena will transform into a four-day crossroads for founders, investors, enterprise leaders, and anyone building or buying technology. The sessions are valuable, but many of the best opportunities happen in hallway conversations and at client dinners. This guide covers the logistics of how to book smart, budget accurately for an international trip, build a realistic conference agenda, and follow up in the most valuble way. What is Web Summit and who is it for? Web Summit is Europe's largest technology conference, hosted annually by Web Summit Ltd. This year, it runs Nov. 9–12, 2026 at Altice Arena (also called MEO Arena) and the Feira Internacional de Lisboa (FIL) exhibition center in Lisbon's Parque das Nações district.[1] The 2026 edition is expected to attract 900-plus speakers, 2,300-plus startups, and 1,200-plus investors from more than 160 countries.[1] General attendee tickets are priced at €1,595, with group discounts available: 10% off for 5–9 tickets 15% off for 10–14 tickets 20% off for 15-plus tickets[1] The crowd spans founders pitching on Centre Stage, investors scanning the startup exhibition, enterprise buyers evaluating SaaS and fintech vendors, developers in specialized tracks, and media covering the week's announcements. If your company sells to technology buyers, raises capital, or partners with startups, a meaningful share of your target market is accessible for four days. November 9 is a pre-conference day featuring badge pickup, mentorship sessions, and opening night. The main conference runs November 10–12, with daily programming from 9 a.m.-5 p.m.[1] Past speakers include Sam Altman (OpenAI), Geoffrey Hinton (University of Toronto), Ursula von der Leyen (European Commission President), Cristiano Amon (Qualcomm CEO), and Alexis Ohanian (Reddit co-founder).[1] Why Web Summit 2026 is worth the trip Web Summit concentrates an unusual density of decision-makers in a four-day window. Your prospect's CTO could be walking the same expo hall. Your integration partner's product lead may be at the same Night Summit event. The investor who passed on your Series A could be attending and open to a conversation over espresso. The conference spans 20-plus content tracks, including dedicated summits for fintech, SaaS, climate tech, marketing, and developer tools.[1] The real value is not only on the main stage. It's in the hallway track, partner dinners, and the conversations that happen after sessions end. Beyond the official agenda, these are some can't-miss happenings: Night Summit , with curated networking events each evening across Lisbon's bars and restaurants Partner-hosted dinners and demo nights in the Chiado, Bairro Alto, and Cais do Sodré neighborhoods 264-plus additional events during Web Summit week, listed on platforms like SideSummit and Luma[2] PITCH competition finals , where early-stage startups present on Centre Stage to global investors Many of the week's best business conversations happen at these side events. The sessions give you context, but the dinners and Night Summit gatherings give you relationships. Plan your trip so you have the energy and calendar space to show up for both. Book your Web Summit flights and hotel early Conference-week hotel prices near Altice Arena climb quickly as Web Summit approaches, making your booking window just as important as your choice of neighborhood. Navan's analysis of hotel bookings from Web Summit 2025 found a median nightly rate of $444 near the venue — roughly 80% higher than a typical October week in Lisbon.[14] Areas in Lisbon with access to Altice Arena Whether you stay within walking distance of the venue or farther away depends on your priorities. Parque das Nações offers the easiest commute, while other neighborhoods can provide lower rates with a short Metro ride. Hotel name Distance to Altice Arena Details Rates Parque das Nações 5-minute walk Flat and modern neighborhood with Vasco da Gama Shopping Centre for essentials Rates are highest during conference week Chiado-Baixa 20 minutes via Metro Access to restaurants, Lisbon's historic center, and direct Red line from Alameda or São Sebastião stations Slightly lower rates than Parque das Nações Avenida da Liberdade 15 minutes via Metro Offers a premium stay outside the conference district, with Metro access via São Sebastião (Red Line) to Oriente High-end hotel options and boutique properties on Lisbon's most elegant boulevard mean higher rates Web Summit hotel pricing and when to book Booking one to two months before check-in offered the best balance of price and availability in Navan's 2025 data. Despite having to pay nearly $100 more per night on average, 40% of conference travelers still booked within two weeks of arrival and 22.9% booked within seven days.[14] Although you can book six or more months out to get your pick of rooms, the rate advantage is less predictable in a smaller sample. Here's when to book based on Navan data from 2025: One to two months out: Median rate of $404, with the best balance of price and availability Two to four weeks out: Median rate of $478, with inventory tightening One to two weeks out: Median rate of $502, as inventory drops Compare any official hotel block against publicly available rates before booking. In some years the conference block offers the best value, but you may find lower prices by booking independently. Flights from the U.S. to Lisbon Lisbon Humberto Delgado Airport (LIS) receives direct flights from several U.S. hubs, including New York/New Jersey (JFK/EWR), Boston, Washington Dulles, and Miami. Flight times range from seven to nine hours, depending on point of origin. For a conference starting Monday, November 9, arriving a day or two early — Saturday, November 7 or Sunday, November 8 — allows time to adjust to the time zone shift before the event begins. How Navan Edge helps with conference travel Navan Edge helps you book flights, hotels, and restaurants in one conversation, backed by AI and 24/7 human travel experts. For Web Summit attendees, Navan Edge lets you compare options across neighborhoods without jumping between booking sites. Triple-dip on hotel stays Navan Edge travelers earn loyalty points from the hotel program, credit card travel rewards, and 5% back in Amazon Gift Cards on eligible hotel stays booked through Navan Edge. On a four-night stay at €200 per night (approximately $870 total), the Amazon Gift Card component amounts to roughly $43 back. Combined, that stacking helps reduce the effective nightly cost . Read Navan Edge's dedicated guide for how to maximize your hotel loyalty points on business trips for a deeper look. Set a realistic Lisbon budget International destinations use per diem rates set by the U.S. State Department rather than domestic General Services Administration (GSA) rates. For Lisbon, the November 2026 allowance is:[4] $350 per day: Includes $249 for lodging and $101 per day for meals and incidental expenses (M&IE) M&IE breakdown: $81 for meals and $20 for incidentals First and last travel days: M&IE drops to 75% of the full rate ($75.75) These rates are effective through December 31, 2026, and can be verified at allowances.state.gov . Budget considerations Now compare that $249 lodging allowance to what Web Summit attendees actually pay. The median nightly rate near Altice Arena during Web Summit 2025 week was $444, a $195-per-night gap between the government allowance and conference-week market rates.[14] Booking one to two months ahead brought the median down to $404, but that still exceeds the per diem cap. If your company reimburses at the State Department rate, you'll likely exceed the reimbursement limit unless you book early or stay in Chiado or Avenida da Liberdade. Be sure to also budget for: Conference ticket: €1,595 (approximately $1,820 USD)[1] Public transportation: Metro from LIS costs €1.90 each way Rideshares and taxis: Uber or Bolt runs €6–10; taxis cost €8–12[5] Daily transit: A daily Viva Viagem pass costs €6.80 and covers Metro, bus, and tram[5] Client dinners: €60–200 per person at Lisbon's business-caliber restaurants After-hours events: Some partner receptions and Night Summit-adjacent dinners carry separate costs beyond the conference ticket Incidentals: Coffee, snacks between sessions, and items you forgot to pack Your $101 daily M&IE allowance goes further in Lisbon than in most U.S. conference cities. A quality lunch near the venue runs €12–18, and a dinner at a locally acclaimed restaurant runs €30–50 per person before drinks. Note: For questions about whether conference travel expenses are tax-deductible, consult a tax professional. Rules vary by jurisdiction and situation. Build your Web Summit agenda in advance Web Summit typically publishes its session catalog several weeks before the conference, and the 1,000-plus speakers across 20-plus tracks creates two common challenges: over-scheduling (eight sessions per day with no gaps) or under-scheduling (winging it and missing the sessions you needed).[1] Most people do best with three to four sessions per day. The Web Summit app is the single most important planning tool. It lets you browse the attendee list, schedule one-on-one meetings, and build a personal agenda before you land in Lisbon.[6] Download it as soon as registration is confirmed. Pre-conference checklist Must-attend keynotes: Centre Stage keynotes set the week's narrative and are recorded, so choose one or two relevant to your role to attend in-person. Workshops and roundtables: These fill fast and are not recorded, making in-person attendance essential. Networking targets: Identify 10–15 specific people you want to meet, send personalized outreach through the app or LinkedIn, and book meetings. Badge pickup: Get your badge on November 9 during the pre-conference period to avoid long queues on the first morning.[6] Book dinner: Confirm meetings with your networking targets and use Navan Edge to book dinner reservations for client meetings before and during Web Summit. Email reminder: Set your out-of-office auto-reply message with return date and emergency contact. Prepare a concise introduction: Be able to explain what you do, why it matters to others, and one specific ask. Cognivix founder Daniele Bernardini, who has attended multiple Web Summits, was quoted on the conference blog, saying, “You should start preparing three months in advance. You should start contacting people, checking who is going to be there … preparation is the best investment of your time, because once you're here, it's too late.”[7] What to wear and pack for Web Summit, Lisbon November highs in Lisbon average 17–19°C (63–66°F) and lows of 11–13°C (52–55°F), with a roughly 24% chance of rain on any given day.[8] The Parque das Nações area, situated along the Tagus River, can feel cooler in the evenings due to waterfront wind. The dress code at Web Summit skews tech-casual, but you should match your audience — not the general crowd. A blazer over a fitted tee works for sessions and most dinners. Enterprise sellers trend slightly more formal, while startup founders trend toward branded hoodies. Web Summit packing list Along with comfortable outfits, we recommend: Two pairs of shoes, including one for dinners and evening events and one for walking, as attendees log 15,000-plus steps daily across venue halls[6] Layers, because temperatures drop after sunset and riverside venues are cooler A waterproof jacket or compact umbrella Chargers for your phone and other devices Noise-canceling earbuds for restful sleep or focus breaks between sessions European power adapter (Type C/F, 230V; U.S. devices need a converter or dual-voltage charger) Snacks, supplements, and vitamins Hand sanitizer and electrolyte packets to stay hydrated and limit germ exposure A passport valid for at least three months beyond your departure date Digital copies of hotel confirmation, conference registration QR code, and transit passes Travel insurance documentation, if necessary Keep your trip documents, hotel confirmations, and flight details accessible in a single chat thread with Navan Edge and eliminate the email-chain scroll when you need your check-in confirmation at the hotel lobby. Your Loyalty Wallet within Navan Edge also stores frequent-flyer and hotel loyalty numbers in one place, simplifying check-in across multiple properties and airlines. Note: U.S. citizens don't need a visa for Portugal. The Schengen area allows stays up to 90 days for tourism and business. Arrival day: Getting from Lisbon Airport to Parque das Nações Lisbon Humberto Delgado Airport (LIS) sits close to the Web Summit venue. The Metro Red Line (Linha Vermelha) runs directly from Aeroporto station to Oriente station (the stop for Parque das Nações) in approximately 10 minutes, at a cost of €1.90 per ride.[5] Trains run every five to eight minutes. Option Duration Cost Best for Metro Red Line (Aeroporto → Oriente) 10 minutes €1.90 Most travelers; fastest and cheapest Uber or Bolt 10–15 minutes €6–10 Heavy luggage, late arrivals Metered taxi 10–15 minutes €8–12 Groups splitting the fare Bus 705 15 minutes €2.30 When Metro is suspended Oriente station is a major transport hub, with direct exits into Vasco da Gama Shopping Centre and the Parque das Nações esplanade.[5] From there, Altice Arena is a five to 10-minute walk along the riverfront. The Web Summit schedule With programming running from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. across Centre Stage, the FIL exhibition halls, and specialized summit tracks, it's important to have a plan. Sessions in Altice Arena and the FIL halls can be a 10-minute walk apart, so build buffer time into your schedule or you'll spend half your day navigating corridors. Consider this agenda: Morning (9–10:30 a.m.): Keynote or one high-priority session, then a scheduled 1:1 meeting over coffee Midday (10:30 a.m.–1 p.m.): Two sessions maximum, with breaks to process and note takeaways Afternoon (1–4 p.m.): Expo floor (startup demos, partner conversations, content track sessions) Evening (5 p.m. onward): One Night Summit event or client dinner Workshops, roundtables, and sessions featuring speakers you want to meet afterward are one of the best uses of your time in person. For the expo floor, head there during Centre Stage keynotes when startup booths are less crowded, rather than immediately after lunch, when foot traffic peaks. If a session conflict means moving your dinner reservation or adding an extra night, Navan Edge handles the change through the same chat where the original booking lives. Indominus Managed Security founder René-Sylvain Bédard, a multi-year attendee, told a reporter for the conference, “You don't actually have time to start learning. You have to go in there and actually know what you want.”[7] Networking that's truly valuable Post-conference connection requests sent within 48 hours outperform those delayed by a week or more, because the conversation is still fresh for both parties. Web Summit networking splits into three phases, and the preparation phase determines the outcome. Before the conference: Build your target list Two weeks before the conference, identify 10–15 specific people to meet with. Look for prospects you've been trying to reach, partners whose product complements yours, and peers in your role at non-competing companies. Use the Web Summit app to browse the attendee list and request 15-minute meetings.[6] A structured pre-event cadence suggests three touchpoints: Day -14 initial outreach Day -7 confirmation Day -1 logistics nudge[9] During the conference: Bring curiosity to the conversation Capture details and context immediately after each conversation: name, company, what you discussed, and what you promised.
